1.title: Course Introduction and Exam Orientation
1.text: Welcome to Module zero: Course Introduction and Exam Orientation. This module covers exam orientation and course map. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do six things. What the dea-C one exam asks, how it is scored and how to book it. The four domains, their weights and the seventeen task statements that this course follows. The kind of question to expect: a data requirement, and the service or setting that fits it best. How the course is built: summaries, a running case, figures, exam tips and practice questions. A study plan and the ground rules for using official sources. --.

1.title: Case Check-In: Meet Kestrel Freight
1.text: Our running case is Kestrel Freight. Meet Kestrel Freight. Trucks send position and temperature readings every few seconds. Warehouses drop order files into storage every night. Customers expect live tracking and correct invoices. Auditors expect to know who saw which data. Your job: build the pipeline, one decision at a time.

1.title: The numbers
1.text: The numbers. The figure shows this: Sixty-five questions of which fifty are scored and fifteen are not, one hundred thirty minutes, a pass mark of seven hundred twenty on a scale of one hundred to one thousand. This fact moves with the A W S pages, so check the current value before you rely on it.

1.title: The numbers, continued
1.text: The numbers, continued. Questions. sixty-five: fifty scored and fifteen unscored (the unscored ones are not marked). Time. one hundred thirty minutes (about two minutes a question). Result. A scaled score from one hundred to one thousand; seven hundred twenty passes; the result is pass or fail. Scoring model. Compensatory: you pass the exam as a whole, not each section. Unanswered. Counted as wrong; there is no penalty for guessing. Fee and format. U S D one hundred fifty; Pearson V U E test center or online proctored; valid three years (as of seven November two thousand twenty-six). Exam tip: Never leave a question blank: a guess costs nothing and a blank always scores zero. This fact moves with the A W S pages, so check the current value before you rely on it.

1.title: Two kinds of question
1.text: Two kinds of question. Multiple choice: one correct answer and three distractors. Multiple response: two or more correct answers out of five or more options; the question says how many to select. Distractors are plausible: services that are real and sometimes useful, but not the best fit for the stated requirement. Exam tip: On multiple response, every correct option must be chosen and no wrong one; read the count in the question ("Select two") before you read the options.

1.title: Who the exam is for
1.text: Who the exam is for. The guide describes a candidate with two to three years of data engineering experience and one to two years of hands-on A W S experience. The exam validates that you can implement data pipelines and monitor, troubleshoot and optimize their cost and performance by best practices. Out of scope for the candidate (so not tested): performing M L (machine learning) training and inference, language-specific syntax, and drawing business conclusions from data. Exam tip: Questions are about choosing and configuring A W S services for a data requirement, not about writing code. Learn what each service is for, what makes it fit, and what makes it a wrong answer.

1.title: Four Domains, Seventeen Task Statements
1.text: Four Domains, Seventeen Task Statements. The figure shows this: The four exam domains and their weights: Ingestion and Transformation thirty-four percent, Data Store Management twenty-six, Operations and Support twenty-two, Security and Governance eighteen.

1.title: Four Domains, Seventeen Task Statements, continued
1.text: Four Domains, Seventeen Task Statements, continued. one Data Ingestion and Transformation. Weight: thirty-four percent. Task statements: one point one Perform data ingestion · one point two Transform and process data · one point three Orchestrate data pipelines · one point four Apply programming concepts. two Data Store Management. Weight: twenty-six percent. Task statements: two point one Choose a data store · two point two Understand data cataloging systems · two point three Manage the lifecycle of data · two point four Design data models and schema evolution. three Data Operations and Support. Weight: twenty-two percent. Task statements: three point one Automate data processing · three point two Analyze data · three point three Maintain and monitor data pipelines · three point four Ensure data quality.

1.title: Four Domains, Seventeen Task Statements, continued
1.text: Four Domains, Seventeen Task Statements, continued. four Data Security and Governance. Weight: eighteen percent. Task statements: four point one Apply authentication mechanisms · four point two Apply authorization mechanisms · four point three Ensure data encryption and masking · four point four Prepare logs for audit · four point five Understand data privacy and governance. The guide lists one hundred twenty skills under the seventeen task statements; this course covers every one of them and nothing else. Domain one is the biggest: about one question in three is about ingesting, transforming, orchestrating or coding a pipeline. The guide is not exhaustive and is updated; A W S publishes changes about one month before the exam reflects them. Exam tip: Spend time in proportion to the weights, but do not skip the small domain: security and governance questions are short and often decided by one setting.

1.title: What changed in guide version 1.1
1.text: What changed in guide version one point one. Published twelve December two thousand twenty-five; the older knowledge and skills lists were merged into one list of skills per task. New skills: integrating large language models (L L M s) for data processing, open table formats such as Apache Iceberg, vector index types (H N S W, I V F (inverted file)) and vectorization, business data catalogs in Amazon SageMaker Catalog, SageMaker Unified Studio domains and projects, and governance frameworks and data sharing patterns.

1.title: What changed in guide version 1.1, continued
1.text: What changed in guide version one point one, continued. Services added to the in-scope list: Amazon Aurora, Amazon Q, Amazon Bedrock, Amazon Kendra, A W S Data Exchange and Amazon S three Tables; removed: A W S Cloud nine, A W S CodeCommit and A W S Schema Conversion Tool as listed services (the skill list still names A W S S C T (Schema Conversion Tool) and A W S D M S (Database Migration Service) Schema Conversion). Exam tip: Older study material may miss the vector, Iceberg, L L M (large language model) and SageMaker Catalog topics. They are in this course because they are in the current guide.

1.title: How This Course Works
1.text: How This Course Works. The figure shows this: Course map: module zero starts the course, then four domain groups hold modules one to five, six to nine, ten to thirteen and fourteen to eighteen, and modules nineteen and twenty close with a recap and exam technique. Modules one to eighteen follow the exam guide: one module per task statement (task one point one has two). Module nineteen is a quick reference with a service chooser; module twenty covers exam technique and a final week.

1.title: How This Course Works, continued
1.text: How This Course Works, continued. Every content module has: what you will learn, a Kestrel Freight case, the content with tables and figures, exam tips, practice questions with explanations, and a quick reference card. Kestrel Freight is a fictional freight and logistics company; its truck telemetry, shipment orders and customer data grow into a data platform, one decision per module. It is fictional and not a real company.

1.title: Labels you will see
1.text: Labels you will see. : A W S changes this often; the item carries an "As of" date, and you should read the A W S page before you rely on it. : a service or feature has a new name, and older questions may use the old one (for example Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose is now Amazon Data Firehose). : taught for understanding, not named in the exam guide. : a date that matters for the exam.

1.title: Study Plan and Ground Rules
1.text: Study Plan and Ground Rules. Study one module, then do its questions; read the quick reference card last. Cover every task statement: the guide does not weight them separately. Compare look-alike services: most wrong answers are real services that fit a different requirement (for example Kinesis Data Streams and Amazon Data Firehose, Athena and Redshift, Glue and E M R (Elastic MapReduce)). Read the requirement words: near real time, lowest cost, least operational overhead, serverless, exactly once, schema-on-read decide the answer. Use the last week for the recap module, the service chooser and exam technique.

1.title: Study Plan and Ground Rules, continued
1.text: Study Plan and Ground Rules, continued. Independence: this course is independent and educational; it is not affiliated with, endorsed or sponsored by Amazon Web Services, and it shows no A W S logos. The A W S exam guide and documentation outrank this course on every fact and rule. Exam tip: Before you book, read A W S's current exam guide and certification page; fees, languages and rules change.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Exam: sixty-five questions (fifty scored, fifteen unscored), one hundred thirty minutes, seven hundred twenty of one thousand to pass, multiple choice and multiple response. Scoring: Compensatory; blank is wrong; guess when unsure. Domains: Ingestion and Transformation thirty-four percent, Data Store Management twenty-six percent, Operations and Support twenty-two percent, Security and Governance eighteen percent. Task statements: seventeen, with one hundred twenty skills; this course covers each once. Guide version: one point one, twelve December two thousand twenty-five: adds L L M s, vectors, Iceberg, SageMaker Catalog. Out of scope: M L training and inference, language syntax, business conclusions. Method: Read the requirement words; compare look-alike services; trust A W S documentation over any course. In the next module, we continue the course.
